- the late-afternoon golden light (ours is now cool midday);
- a canal or river with bridges and bumboats through the district;

The Supertrees are crude: cylinders with cubic leaf clusters.

I viewed only the A/B images and context.txt files. The in-development frames show a coherent Singapore-like world: the landmark analogues show good intent, and the trees, water and boat wakes are decent. They lose for four reasons that repeat across every frame: (1) flat, high-key midday lighting under a uniform pale haze, with weak shadow contrast and no light sources; (2) cloned, pristine building kits, generic slab skylines and placeholder geometry (the untextured grey box in pair 2); (3) nearly empty streets, with sparse traffic and no pedestrians; (4) chase cameras that either centre the helicopter so it blocks the view or pitch so steeply at the rooftops that the city reads as a city-builder or tilt-shift miniature. The placeholder-looking minimaps add to the impression. The references win mainly on lighting (backlit golden smog, dusk light from windows and streets, a volumetric searchlight), on composition (foreground silhouettes, leading lines, a hero aircraft against the sky) and on dense, believable variety. The fixes with the most leverage, in order: a dramatic time-of-day and lighting pass with graded aerial perspective and visible lights; variety and weathering of the building kit plus removal of placeholder geometry; traffic and pedestrian density; and camera framing that keeps the horizon and a readable helicopter in frame. The references are curated marketing stills (some with logos, no HUD) compared against HUD-on gameplay captures, which widens the gap somewhat but would not flip any verdict. Only pair 3 B and pair 4 A genuinely wow; no in-development frame does.
